title: A Fast Exact Algorithm to Enumerate Maximal Pseudo-cliques in Large Sparse Graphs

problem.claim: Efficiently enumerating pseudo-cliques is difficult because they do not satisfy the convertible antimonotone constraint, making search-space reduction hard.

gap.claim: The two previously proposed exact algorithms, ODES and PCE, have high execution times.

contributions.claim: Presents FPCE, an exact algorithm for enumerating maximal pseudo-cliques.
Introduces pruning techniques to reduce the pseudo-clique search space.
Applies FPCE to a PPI network to identify pseudo-cliques.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across 15 real and 16 synthetic graphs, FPCE was reported to be faster on average than ODES and PCE by the stated factors.
On a PPI network, FPCE outputs were reported to match more known protein complexes and to be more accurate and biologically more significant than those of a popular heuristic method.
The authors report that FPCE's speed makes it suitable for such cases.

narrative_sequence.summary: Their constraint properties make search-space reduction and efficient enumeration difficult, while existing exact algorithms have high execution times.
The paper presents FPCE, an exact enumerator using derived pruning techniques.
Experiments compare FPCE with ODES and PCE on real and synthetic graphs and apply it to a PPI network against a heuristic method.
The authors report speed advantages and more favorable PPI-network output properties for FPCE.

source_observation.claim: The absence of a convertible antimonotone constraint makes pseudo-clique search-space reduction difficult.

interpretation.claim: When standard monotone pruning structure is unavailable, specialized pruning techniques may be needed.

application.claim: For enumeration problems with difficult search-space reduction, investigate problem-specific pruning rules.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when these pruning techniques may fail or generalize beyond pseudo-clique enumeration.

source_observation.claim: The reported exact method was faster than prior exact algorithms and produced favorable results against a heuristic method on a PPI network.

interpretation.claim: Exact computation can be practically useful when algorithmic efficiency is sufficient.

application.claim: Consider exact methods for applied network analysis when their runtime supports the target use case.

exception.claim: The abstract does not report runtime requirements, scalability limits, or whether the findings extend beyond the evaluated graphs and PPI application.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal definition of maximal pseudo-cliques.
The abstract does not describe the pruning techniques or algorithmic complexity.
The abstract does not provide absolute runtimes, graph characteristics, or evaluation protocols.
The abstract does not identify the heuristic method or detail the biological significance analysis.
